title: Choir and Crown
premise: Vesper Amberdale, a bone-carver whose carvings let her hear the voices of the dead, is given a dying courier's map to the Hollow Choir — a vault beneath the Thornfells where the last true king's memory-song lies sealed, the only thing that can either legitimize or destroy the usurper Queen Maren's fragile peace. Hunted by the Queen's Inquisitor Corvane, who wants the song destroyed, and shadowed by Aldric, a disgraced royalist knight who wants it crowned, Vesper must decide whether the dead king's voice should rule the living. She learns the 'song' is actually the imprisoned memories of thousands slaughtered in the ancient war, kept singing to power the capital's wards. In the end, Vesper refuses both crown and destruction: she frees the dead by carving their names into living bone, collapsing the wards and forcing the realm to face its buried past — and chooses love with Aldric over any throne.
about_author: Quentin Fairweather is the pen name of a former cathedral stonemason turned novelist who lives somewhere along the Welsh marches with two ill-tempered goats. Their fiction blends folk-horror atmosphere with quietly political fantasy about ordinary craftspeople caught in history's gears.

chapters.title: The Listening Bone
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the market town of Greyhollow, Vesper carves a memorial whistle for a grieving widow and hears the dead man's last words through it — establishing her gift and its cost: every voice stays with her. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; she trusts the dead more than the living.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A bleeding courier collapses at her workshop door, presses a bone-cased map into her hands, and dies whispering 'the Choir still sings.' Royalist riders arrive searching for it. Beat: terror and reluctant responsibility as she hides the map inside a half-carved femur.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Using her knowledge of the Thornfell smuggler roads, Vesper slips past the first checkpoint, guided by the map's impossible detail — it shows tunnels that shouldn't exist. Beat: grim exhilaration; for once her outlaw knowledge is worth something more than survival.

chapters.title: The Knight Without a Banner
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Disgraced royalist knight Aldric intercepts Vesper on the mountain road but lets her go, torn between duty to the old bloodline and disgust at what royalists have become. Beat: honor at war with itself; he begins following her not to take the map but to understand it.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper returns secretly to Greyhollow and learns from the widow's carved keepsake that the dead courier had visited her before — carrying messages for someone in the palace. Inquisitor Corvane arrives, courteous and terrifying. Beat: dread; the hunt has a face now.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Inquisitor interrogates Greyhollow gently, burning nothing, threatening no one — and gets everything. He believes destroying the Choir's song is mercy, having seen what war-memory does to minds. Beat: chilling sympathy; the antagonist is almost right.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Sheltering in a flooded mountain chapel, Vesper carves a fragment of the map's casing and hears the courier's ghost describe the Choir: not a treasure, a prison of voices. Aldric catches up and offers alliance instead of arrest. Beat: wary trust kindling into something warmer.

chapters.title: Two Roads Down
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Vesper and Aldric travel together, trading histories — his fall from grace after refusing an order, her mother's disappearance into the mountains years ago. The map's tunnels begin matching her mother's old carvings. Beat: intimacy deepening; personal stakes braid into political ones.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At a smuggler toll-gate, the price of passage is a name spoken aloud — and the gatekeeper recognizes Vesper's mother's name on the map's margin. Her mother was the Choir's last keeper. Beat: betrayal and revelation; Vesper realizes she was always meant to inherit this.

chapters.title: Maren's Empty Throne
chapters.summary: Queen Maren's POV. In the capital, the wards flicker for the first time in a century. Maren, a usurper who genuinely rules well, learns the song sustains her peace and orders Corvane to find it before the royalists do. Beat: the weight of borrowed power; even good rule rests on theft.

chapters.title: Ambush at Sorrow Bridge
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Royalist hardliners ambush the pair, wanting the song to crown a pretender king. Aldric kills former comrades to save Vesper and is gravely wounded. Beat: love confessed under blood; there is no neutral ground left for him.

chapters.title: Bone-Set and Bone-Song
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. While setting Aldric's broken arm, Vesper carves a splint from the map's casing and accidentally releases the courier's full memory: the Choir holds ten thousand war-dead, still conscious, still singing. Beat: horror reframing everything; the secret isn't a weapon, it's people.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following her mother's carvings, Vesper finds the hidden door beneath the Thornfells — and her mother's skeleton beside it, dead for twenty years, still holding a chisel. Through the bone, her mother's voice finally speaks. Beat: grief and inheritance; the dead give her the choice they never finished making.

chapters.title: Inside the Choir
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They enter the vault: a cavern of suspended bones humming with ten thousand overlapping voices, each ward-stone in the capital fed by this endless grief. Vesper hears individual names, individual pleas. Beat: awe curdling into moral vertigo; the peace above is built on suffering below.

chapters.title: The Pretender's Mass
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The royalist faction reaches the vault, led by Lord Cassel, who plans to bind the song to a puppet king. Aldric openly breaks with his order, declaring the dead are not a crown. Beat: open rebellion; Aldric chooses Vesper and conscience over restoration.

chapters.title: Corvane Descends
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Inquisitor arrives with the Queen's warrant to burn the vault, revealing he once freed a smaller choir and watched the resulting plague of unanchored memories kill a valley. Beat: tragic conviction; his solution would work and be unforgivable.

chapters.title: Three Hands on One Chisel
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cornered between Cassel's binding ritual and Corvane's fire, Vesper proposes a third way: carve each name into new bone, giving every dead soul an anchor outside the vault. It will take days they don't have as the wards above begin failing. Beat: desperate hope; craft as resistance.

chapters.title: The Long Carving
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. An improbable truce: royalists, inquisitors, and smugglers all labor at Vesper's bench as the mountain shakes. Cassel sabotages the work; Aldric stops him at the cost of a hand. Beat: sacrifice and solidarity; enemies become witnesses.

chapters.title: When the Song Stops
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The last name is carved as the vault collapses. Ten thousand voices pass through Vesper at once — every death, every name — and then go quiet, free. The capital's wards fail, but no war comes: only a kingdom suddenly able to remember honestly. Beat: transcendence through loss; Veper carries the silence like a scar.

chapters.title: The Queen's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. With the wards down, Maren must confess how her peace was powered or watch it crumble. She chooses confession, abdicating claim to the old bloodline's legitimacy and offering elected councils instead. Corvane, undone, walks into the mountains. Beat: power relinquished; corruption refused at the last door.

chapters.title: Choir and Crown
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Months later, Greyhollow builds a hall of carved names — a choir that asks nothing of the living. Aldric, one-handed, apprentices himself to her bench. Offered honors, Vesper declines them all. Beat: quiet resolution; love chosen over duty, memory honored over power.

chapters.title: The Next Voice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. A child arrives at the workshop holding a bone that whispers — the gift passing to a new generation. Vesper begins teaching her not to fear the dead, only to serve them well. Final beat: continuity and hope; the story ends where listening begins.
